problem_statement: When a border router changes its local on-link prefix (for example, after an extended PAN ID change) it continues to advertise the old on-link prefix as a deprecated prefix in its router advertisements. However, if another router on the infrastructure link is actively advertising that same prefix as a preferred (non-deprecated) on-link prefix, the border router should not keep advertising it as deprecated, because the two advertisements conflict. Currently the border router keeps emitting the old prefix as a deprecated prefix even though another router is advertising it as preferred, and it resumes deprecating it whenever that router stops advertising it as preferred.
